summary: Nielsen Norman Group article summarizing research on how readers react when AI use in text content is disclosed, and proposing the PACED framework (Policy, Audience, Context, Expectations, Degree of AI use) for deciding whether to disclose. It covers the EU AI Act transparency obligations, the difference between disclosures and watermarks, mixed study results, the 'disclosure paradox', and the finding that third-party exposure is penalized most. The article is about AI-generated text content and disclosure, not about how people operate computers.
speakers_or_authors: Nielsen Norman Group (UX research practitioners); summarizes studies by Licenji and Hoxha, Purcell et al., Li et al., Nakano et al., Brüns and Meißner, Sahebi et al., Fang et al., Schilke and Reimann.
relevance_reason: It concerns disclosure of AI-generated text and reader trust, not personal-context devices, computer-use agents, or voice and conversational interfaces. It is only loosely related to AI interface design, and its research evidence is about content labels rather than how people interact with computers.

claims.claim: Across the reviewed research, there was no single consistent audience reaction to AI disclosure; effects varied by context.
claims.quote: Across the experiments and reports we reviewed for this article, there wasn’t one consistent audience reaction to AI disclosure.

claims.claim: In a trust game with real money, labeling messages as AI-assisted did not reduce money sent or trustworthiness ratings.
claims.quote: The AI disclosure did not reduce either how much money message recipients sent or their rating of the other person’s trustworthiness.

claims.claim: Readers say they want AI use disclosed yet rate disclosed AI content less favorably (the 'disclosure paradox').
claims.quote: The disclosure paradox refers to readers saying they want AI use disclosed, yet reacting negatively to content that carries that disclosure.

claims.claim: Having AI use exposed by a third party produced the lowest trust, so proactive disclosure may be safer.
claims.quote: Their final experiment revealed they trusted one whose AI use was exposed by a third party least of all.

claims.claim: The EU AI Act transparency obligations for disclosing AI-generated content began in August 2026.
claims.quote: the transparency obligations started in August 2026.

commercial_interest: None apparent beyond NN/g's consulting and training business; no product being promoted.
older_event: Not mainly about an older event; it summarizes recent 2024-2026 research and the August 2026 EU transparency obligations.
